 4m ago 23.24 EST Democrat Rob Sand wins governor's race in Iowa
 Democrat Rob Sand has won the governor’s race in Iowa, beating Republican businessman Zach Lahn .
 Sand, Iowa’s state auditor, ran on a moderate platform, courting voters who were disillusioned by the Trump agenda affected by the administration’s sweeping tariffs and the hike in fuel prices as a result of the Iran war. Sand is also the first Democrat to be elected to the governor’s mansion in the Hawkeye state since 2006. 
 Share 5m ago 23.23 EST Latest midterm results
 Democrats have seen historic victories in tonight’s midterm elections. Although Donald Trump has blamed Republican losses on the fact that he was not on the ballot, he said will accept the results of tonight’s elections.
 Here are the latest results:
 Democrat James Talarico has won the US Senate race in Texas, securing an astonishing and historic victory. Talarico, a state representative, beat the scandal-plagued attorney general, Ken Paxton in the most expensive race of this midterms cycle. Talarico is also the first Democrat to win a US Senate seat in the Lone Star state since 1988.
 Democrat Gina Hinojosa has won the governor’s race in Texas, beating the Republican incumbent Greg Abbott – who is serving his third-term. Hinojosa makes history as Texas’ first Latina governor , and the first Democrat to occupy the governor’s mansion since 1990.
 Democrat Sherrod Brown has won the US Senate special election in Ohio, beating Republican incumbent Jon Husted . Brown, who lost his 2024 race, launched a comeback this year to finish out the rest of JD Vance’s Senate term – which ends in 2029.
 Democrat Amy Acton has won the Ohio governor’s race, beating Republican Vivek Ramaswamy , the Donald Trump-backed Republican nominee. It’s a stunning blow to Republicans, after the gubernatorial race turned rancorous just weeks ago when Ramaswamy released an ad featuring Acton’s estranged mother – who hasn’t seen her daughter since she was removed from her custody when she was 12.
 Deb Haaland , the former interior secretary under Joe Biden, has been elected governor of New Mexico and will become the first Native American woman to govern a US state.
 Democrat Janelle Stelson has won the race for Pennsylvania’s 10th congressional district, beating hardline conservative Scott Perry – the four-term incumbent.
 Democrat Paige Cognetti has won Pennsylvania’s eighth congressional district, beating Republican incumbent Rob Bresnahan – who flipped the seat in 2024.
 Share 11m ago 23.17 EST Democrat Gina Hinojosa wins governor's race in Texas, makes history as state's first Latina governor
 Democrat Gina Hinojosa has won the governor’s race in Texas, beating the Republican incumbent Greg Abbott – who is serving his third-term.
 Hinojosa makes history as Texas’ first Latina governor , and the first Democrat to occupy the governor’s mansion since 1990.
 It’s the second stunning upset of the night in the Lone Star state, after James Talarico made history as the first Democrat to win a US Senate seat in nearly 40 years.
 Share 11m ago 23.17 EST Democrat Sherrod Brown wins US Senate race in Ohio, flipping seat
 Democrat Sherrod Brown has won the US Senate special election in Ohio, beating Republican incumbent Jon Husted .
 Brown, who lost his 2024 race, launched a comeback this year to finish out the rest of JD Vance’s Senate term – which ends in 2029.
 Share 14m ago 23.15 EST Texas governor Greg Abbott has conceded his race for re-election. The Associated Press has not yet called the results of Texas’ governor’s race.
 View image in fullscreen Greg Abbott speaks to supporters at an election night event in Austin, Texas. Photograph: David J Phillip/AP “After looking at all the details of every county in the entire state, I made the decision to go ahead and call Gina Hinojosa and congratulate her on winning this race for governor of the state of Texas,” Abbott said at his watch party. “There are still votes to be counted, but mathematically we’re not going to be able to win this election.”
 Share Updated at  23.24 EST 16m ago 23.12 EST Robert Tait in Portland, Maine 
 Chellie Pingree , the Democratic representative for Maine, is celebrating being elected for a 10th term in an election she told celebrating fellow Democrats felt” “different” to what she had previously encountered.
 Talking to the Guardian, she said widespread disgust with Donald Trump ’s policies had united Democrats with disaffected Republicans and independents in a groundswell that could lead to the unseating of the state’s long-serving GOP senator Susan Collins , who was trailing her Democratic challenger Troy Jackson in early returns.
 “Donald Trump has uniquely managed to make Republicans , Democrats, and Independents mad at him, and so it’s not just Democrats who are voting tonight,” Pingree said. “It’s Republicans who are so mad they’re not coming out. Independents who are voting for Democrats and people who are just saying we’ve got to have some change in our country, and the Republicans haven’t been fighting back. So we’re seeing a real repudiation of the presidents and the Republicans who’ve gone along with him.”
 Referring to Collins, who has been a senator for 30 years and has fought off previous robust challenges when polls indicated she was vulnerable, Pingree said: “Mainers have been very engaged and very angry, and have come out to vote in record numbers and I think if she loses tonight, is because people feel that we’ve been armed by the policies of Donald Trump, and the Republicans haven’t done enough to fight back.”
 Asked if a Democrat-run Congress would try to impeach Trump, who was impeached twice during his first presidency, she said: “I don’t think impeachment will be the first thing we try to do. I think there are so many important things we need to investigate. So many funding streams we need to reverse. I just think people will feel like we have a big agenda, and unless we’re confident of convicting him in the Senate, I doubt that we’ll bring up impeachment.”
 Share 21m ago 23.08 EST Nancy Pelosi, the Democratic former House speaker, said “the American people have changed the course of our country ”, in a statement tonight. 
 “By electing a Democratic House Majority, they have broken Washington’s Republican monopoly on power and restored a constitutional check on a President who has governed as though none should exist,” she said.
 Pelosi added, “With tremendous personal pride, I congratulate our next Speaker, Hakeem Jeffries . Exactly twenty years after I became the first woman to hold the gavel, he will make history as the first Black Speaker of the House.”
 Share Updated at  23.08 EST 22m ago 23.06 EST Dara Kerr in Commerce City, Colorado 
 With a big American flag as his backdrop and a jubilant crowd, Manny Rutinel started his victory speech saying: “This election was decided at kitchen tables.”
 The 31-year-old democrat, who’s slated to cinch a victory for a toss-up congressional seat in Central Colorado, looked over at his mom standing next to him on the stage and said it started 20 years ago at a kitchen table with her – as they sorted through bills trying to figure out how to make ends meet.
 “Do people like us count?” Rutinel said. “In the wealthiest nation in the world, do people like me and my mom matter?”
 The crowd went wild. Rutinel, who ran his campaign on affordability and fighting corruption in Washington, said that hundreds of thousands of Colorado voters sat at kitchen tables and filled out their ballots. He had to pause, filled with emotion.
 “Neither a trillionaire nor the president of the US could buy this election,” Rutinel said, alluding to the millions in Super Pac funding from Elon Musk, Donald Trump and Charles Koch that poured into his competitor Gabe Evan’s campaign.
 “Colorado, from the bottom of my heart, thank you,” Rutinel said.

 Democrat James Talarico has won the US Senate race in Texas, securing an astonishing and historic victory. 
 Talarico, a state representative, beat the scandal-plagued attorney general, Ken Paxton in the most expensive race of this midterms cycle.
 Talarico is also the first Democrat to win a US Senate seat in the Lone Star state since 1988.
 Share 26m ago 23.03 EST California and other west coast states close polls
 Polls have now closed in California, where former health secretary Xavier Becerra , a Democrat, has defeated Republican Steve Hilton , a former adviser to British prime minister David Cameron, in the race for governor.
 Most polls will also close in Oregon, along with all polls in Washington state.
 In Washington, two-term Democrat Marie Gluesenkamp Perez, who has frequently broken with her party on key issues, is hoping to hold on to her seat in a district that Trump carried in each of the last three presidential elections.
 Share 27m ago 23.02 EST Trump says he will accept election results
 Donald Trump says he will accept the results of tonight’s elections. 
 In an interview with the New York Times, Trump said he was “absolutely willing to accept those results.”
 “We’ll, you know, look forward to working with them,” he said of working with Democrats . “We’ll probably work something out.”
 Share 33m ago 22.55 EST Deb Haaland wins in New Mexico, making history as first female Native American governor
 Deb Haaland , the former interior secretary under Joe Biden, has been elected governor of New Mexico and will become the first Native American woman to govern a US state.
 Haaland, a Democrat, defeated her Republican opponent Gregg Hull, a businessman and the longtime mayor of the city of Rio Rancho.
